transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-09
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya D. (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Mark H., Sofia A., Tom B., Priya K., Eli T.

Summary: Kickoff for activation and handoff from sales to success/engineering. Covered staging plan, security requirements (SOC2, KMS), networking (VPC peering), performance expectations (4k token sequences, tail latency), dedicated vs hosted options, rollout plan and next steps.

[00:00] Jared (Redwood): Okay everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jared from Redwood, and with me is Priya our SE and Lena from success. This call is to kick off the activation and make sure we have the handoff details. Mark, do you want to open with priorities?

[00:19] Mark (Northfield): Sure, yeah thanks. Um, main goal is to get a pilot running in our dev VPC by mid-November, and then a canary into prod in early December. Top requirements are data residency — all inference logs need to stay in our region — and encryption via KMS. We'll also need SOC2 evidence for the hosted path, though we're open to the dedicated pool if costs line up.

[00:42] Priya D. (Redwood SE): Got it. When you say pilot, are you planning to use the hosted Redwood API initially or go straight to private deployment?

[00:52] Sofia (Northfield): We want to try hosted for dev to move faster, but our security team is wary — they might ask for a private VPC or dedicated capacity for production. So the staging needs to mirror prod networking as much as possible.

[01:10] Priya K. (Security): Right, and on that note, we'll need SAML SSO, RBAC controls, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also can you confirm how KMS integration works — do we bring our own key or is it Redwood-managed?

[01:25] Jared: Great questions. We support both: bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) with HSM-backed keys, and Redwood-managed keys. We'll share the integration guide — it outlines the KMS fingerprint exchange, key policies, and HSM support. For SAML SSO we have a runbook and SSO metadata export. I'll make sure Lena drops those links after the call.

[01:42] Speaker 1 (unclear): sorry, is there anything about PII redaction at rest?

[01:46] Priya D.: We have built-in redactors at the prompt layer, but for storage we recommend tokenization before logs leave your VPC. Also we can turn off retention for certain routes — retention is configurable per-route in the console.

[02:05] Tom (CTO): On performance: our main use-case is a multi-turn assistant that often hits 3.5k to 4k tokens. Tail latency above 700ms is problematic for some flows. What realistic latency should we expect on your hosted service vs Dedicated?

[02:22] Priya D.: For a 4k seq on a large open model, hosted will be around 600–1200ms tail depending on load and batching; Dedicated gives more predictable tails — 350–700ms typically if you reserve the right GPU profile and pin the model. There's variance depending on quantization and kv cache access. Also, batching helps cost but can increase tail if not configured carefully.

[02:48] Mark: So this is the tradeoff we discussed with the execs — cost vs. consistency. If we start hosted then move to dedicated, how disruptive is model pinning/rollout?

[02:58] Priya D.: Rollouts are designed to be non-disruptive. You can pin model versions and we support canary traffic split. We also have an automated fallback policy to a compatible quantized variant if the primary model is out of capacity. You won't need client changes for standard SDK routes, but we'll validate latency SLAs during the pilot.

[03:20] Lena (Redwood CSM): We'll also provide a checklist for staging that lists the config flags you'll want to set to match prod routing and cache behaviors.

[03:30] Sofia: Can we talk briefly about observability? We need token-level cost attribution and traces for certain customer flows.

[03:36] Jared: Yes — Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-route latency heatmaps, and you can export traces. We can ship a sample dashboard and the analytics event schema.

[03:50] Eli: What's the typical uplift in cost when you enable continuous KV caching and aggressive batching? We want to understand unit economics.

[03:58] Priya D.: KV caching usually reduces token compute for repeated prefixes — so it reduces cost on steady-state sessions, but adds a small memory footprint. Aggressive batching can push amortized cost down 10–40% depending on distribution, but at the expense of tail. We'll run a suggested config based on your session distribution.

[04:20] Mark: Good — please include an example with our expected 60% short sessions and 40% long multi-turn sessions.

[04:28] Priya D.: Noted. We'll use your sample logs. Can you share anonymized request traces?

[04:33] Mark: Yes, we can share a redacted sample later today.

[04:38] [05:02] -- brief cross talk --

[05:10] Priya K. (Security): For compliance, we need SOC 2 artifacts and pen test reports. Also, our internal legal will want a data processing addendum.

[05:20] Jared: We have a SOC 2 Type II report and can provide a pen test summary; full reports under NDA. We also provide a DPA template. Lena will attach the security pack.

[05:31] Tom: On networking — VPC peering is preferred. Do you support private link / transit gateway or only peering?

[05:38] Priya D.: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink options; transit gateway usually works too but we'll coordinate with infra. Peering is simplest for the pilot. For Private deployments we can ship a customer-managed control plane with full VPC controls.

[05:52] Eli: Any special firewall ports or egress rules we should be aware of?

[05:56] Priya D.: Outbound TLS to the control plane, and a couple of ports for health checks; we'll provide a minimal firewall guide.

[06:05] [06:30] -- 6 minute marker --

[06:35] Mark: Ok timeline recap — pilot in dev by mid-November, canary in early December. Our questions: 1) What's blocking you from starting the pilot this week? 2) What do you need from us?

[06:49] Jared: From Redwood side, we'll need the VPC details, the BYOK fingerprint if you choose BYOK, and your anonymized traces for batching recommendations. We'll also run an initial bench to give you expected latency numbers.

[07:01] Priya D.: Technically, I'll spin up a dedicated bench environment and run the 4k seq tests. Expect a first pass within one week of receiving the sample and network info.

[07:14] Sofia: How do we handle logging — can logs be forwarded to our S3 in-region or must stay in Redwood's storage?

[07:23] Priya D.: You can forward logs: we support S3 delivery to customer buckets, or streaming via your ingestion pipeline. For hosted, logs can optionally be stored only in your bucket with no retention on Redwood side. For Private, logs always stay in your environment.

[07:37] Priya K.: Are you able to show chain-of-custody for keys and who accessed logs? We need auditability for PCI/PHI workflows.

[07:44] Jared: Yes — audit logs include key access events, admin actions, and route-level config changes. We can map those events into your SIEM format. We'll include the event schema.

[07:55] [08:20] -- short pause while someone reads a doc --

[08:35] Priya D.: Quick note on deployment patterns: for latency-critical routes, we recommend model pinning to a dedicated worker group and pre-warmed kv caches. For cost-sensitive ephemeral workloads, the hosted auto-scaling path with caching off is usually cheaper.

[08:57] Mark: Regarding model variants—will clients need to change prompts when switching quantized variants? We've had odd hallucination differences in other stacks.

[09:07] Priya D.: Usually no prompt changes for compatible variants, but small behavioral drifts can occur. We run a prompt evaluation suite — Redwood Optimize — to detect regressions against a provided eval set. We'll include that in the pilot so you can catch regressions early.

[09:24] Lena: We'll schedule a Redwood Optimize walkthrough as part of the pilot cadence.

[09:30] Sofia: For the pilot, what's the expected support SLAs? We need an escalation path for incidents in the dev -> prod ramp.

[09:40] Jared: For customers onboarding to Dedicated or Private we offer higher SLAs and a named technical contact. During the pilot you'll have standard support plus triage calls; if you convert to an enterprise contract we'll assign a dedicated support engineer.

[09:54] Tom: Any limitations on model size or custom model imports? We plan to try a fine-tuned open model and possibly bring a tuned checkpoint.

[10:05] Priya D.: We support bringing your own compatible checkpoints; however, the runtime needs a small conversion step and some kernel selection preferences. We'll include a checklist for model onboarding and recommended quantization profiles.

[10:18] [10:40] -- 10 minute marker, flow keeps going --

[10:45] Mark: Let's lock down immediate next steps. We'll: 1) send redacted traces and sample prompts, 2) decide whether to BYOK or use Redwood-managed KMS, 3) provide VPC info. What do you need from Redwood?

[10:59] Priya D.: The bench will need an example request load profile and a small script to replay sessions. Also the security pack and runbook. Lena will attach those.

[11:08] Lena: I'll share three docs after the call: onboarding runbook, security pack (SOC2/pen test summary and DPA), and an initial staging checklist with checkboxes for SSO, KMS, VPC, and observability hooks.

[11:21] Eli: One more question — are there any gotchas for Kubernetes-based tooling on our side? We run model orchestration inside our EKS clusters.

[11:29] Priya D.: Most integrations are agnostic; if you want to host the model privately inside EKS we'll provide a lightweight runtime image and helm chart. For production-grade GPU workloads we usually recommend dedicated GPU nodes or specialized inference hosts.

[11:43] Mark: That helps. Ok, any other risks we should call out?

[11:48] Priya K.: My team flagged data residency and key ownership as the top risk; if BYOK can't be demonstrated we may require Private deployment which impacts timeline.

[11:57] Jared: Understood. We'll prioritize a BYOK walkthrough in the security deep-dive. If BYOK isn't viable, we'll map out the Private deployment path and timeline.

[12:06] [12:30] -- near end --

[12:35] Final recap (Jared): 1) Redwood to share runbook, security pack, and staging checklist by 2026-10-12. 2) Northfield to share redacted traces and VPC details by 2026-10-14. 3) Redwood SE to run bench once samples arrive and deliver initial latency/throughput by 2026-10-16. 4) Schedule security deep-dive (week of 2026-10-19).

[12:58] Mark: That aligns with our internal milestones. We'll aim to have the artifacts to you in the next 48 hours.

[13:05] Priya K.: I'll coordinate on the SOC2 and BYOK checklist and follow up with legal.

[13:12] Lena: I'll send calendar invites for the deep-dive and attach the documents.

[13:18] Jared: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with the links and the action items.

[13:25] Tom: Thanks everyone.

[13:28] -- meeting ends --

Notes on transcript quality: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and a couple of hyphenations; speaker 1 was an unclear attendee and was left as-is. Some technical terms (KV cache, BYOK, PrivateLink) were transcribed phonetically at times.
